lines.trans: I followed you because I fell in love with your talent as a director.
Please shoot another film with Kuroki that surpasses her debut.
If you cannot do that, I am firing you.
You think you can fire me—Toru Muranishi?
I am the president of this company, so I hold that authority!
Mr. Kawada, what is it that you yourself want to create?
All you ever do is stand in the back and watch.

words.gram: Colloquial contraction of だろう after past tense た.

lines.trans: I always stand at the front and do what nobody else has ever done.
Why are you so obsessed with being number one even at such huge risk!
Because I have never been number one before.

words.gram: Past た-form of なる (to become).

lines.trans: The era of videotape will end. Those who miss the next wave have no future.
Mr. Kawada or me—follow whichever one of us you believe you can trust.

words.gram: て-form of auxiliary くる (go do something and return), used as a soft request.

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 僕はあなたの監督としての才能にほれてついてきたんだ。
examples.trans: I followed you because I fell in love with your talent as a director.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
あの作品を超えるのはそう簡単じゃありません。
examples.trans: Surpassing that debut film of ours won't be easy.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.

examples.text: それができないなら、私はあなたを解雇します。
examples.trans: If you cannot do that, I am firing you.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: クビにできるんですか？この私を。
examples.trans: You think you can fire me—Toru Muranishi?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Directly modifies a noun near the speaker (この店, この辺, この部分).

examples.text: この本は人気があります。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Everyday word for a business company or one's workplace.

examples.text: 新しい会社に入りました。

examples.trans: The company is near the station.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').

examples.text: 私はこの会社の社長です。だからその権限がある！
examples.trans: I am the president of this company, so I hold that authority!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 私は常に先頭に立って、まだ誰もやったことのないことをやる。
examples.trans: I always stand at the front and do what nobody else has ever done.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: In 頭が切れる, means 'sharp-minded / clever'.
Godan verb; in 役に立つ, means 'to be useful'.

examples.text: ここに立ってください。
この経験はきっと役に立ちます。
examples.trans: This experience will surely be useful.

meanings.note: Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。
どうしてそんなに危険を冒してでも一番にこだわるんですか！
examples.trans: Why are you so obsessed with being number one even at such huge risk!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: どうしてそんなに危険を冒してでも一番にこだわるんですか！
examples.trans: Why are you so obsessed with being number one even at such huge risk!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。
俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 時代が変わりましたね。

meanings.note: Noun derived from 終わる (to end).

examples.text: これで今日の授業は終わりです。
examples.trans: With this, today's class is over.

examples.text: ビデオの時代は終わります。乗り遅れた人に未来はない。
examples.trans: The era of videotape will end. Those who miss the next wave have no future.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。
ビデオの時代は終わります。乗り遅れた人に未来はない。
examples.trans: The era of videotape will end. Those who miss the next wave have no future.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
